messages:
Sam: heads up — after yesterday's async-batcher kernel-selection tweak I’m seeing short requests P95 jump ~3x when they run mixed with long sequences. repro on canary. :eyes:
PerfBot: [perf-regression] batcher_v2 deploy @ 2024-06-25T10:12Z. Metric: short-path P95 up 3.1x, overall throughput steady.
Anya: ugh. can you paste the profiling snapshot? flamegraph / traces?
Sam: putting links — flamegraph + perf trace: https://perf.internal/fg/1719504321 , trace: https://perf.internal/trace/1719504321
Sam: quick notes from the trace:
- batch formation shows long seqs monopolizing the "token budget" bucket, causing short requests to sit in queue and get coalesced into huge backfilled batches -> cold-kernel path for shorts
- KV cache hit-rate on mixed load drops from 87% -> 65% (per-tenant sample) which increases compute and shifts kernel selection to slower kernels
Mike: that aligns with what I feared — our batcher now greedily fills batches by token budget instead of respecting short-path reservation.
Anya: what config values are we using?
Sam: current canary config (snippet):
```
batcher.max_tokens_per_batch = 4096
batcher.token_target = 512
batcher.wait_ms = 8
queue.per_tenant_token_reserve = 0.0  # default, no short reservation
short_path_threshold_tokens = 32
```
Sam: proposal: add a small short-path reservation and a per-tenant soft cap to prevent long sequences from consuming all tokens. e.g. reserve 10-20% of token budget for requests <= short_path_threshold_tokens.
Anya: can you show a quick pseudo of the admission change?
Sam: sure:
```python
# pseudo admission: called when request arrives
if req.tokens <= SHORT_THRESH:
    reserved = max(global_short_reserve, per_tenant_short_reserve[req.tenant])
    if batch.available_tokens < reserved:
        route_to_short_fastlane(req)
        return
# otherwise fall back to normal enqueue
enqueue(req)
```
Mike: also suggest bounding long-sequence per-tenant burst: per_tenant_token_cap = 2048 (sliding window). prevents single tenant long-run from starving others.
Leo: FYI telemetry: when mixes occur we see KV warmup churn — long sequences flush or evict hot KV entries because they extend cache window, so short requests lose prefix hits. Could consider KV-priority pins for short-key prefixes.
Tia: thought: instead of absolute reserve, we could use dynamic credit smoothing: refill short-lane credits at a steady rate and allow borrowing only if short credit pool > 0. That keeps long jobs from permanently starving shorts.
Anya: love that. can we A/B both approaches? short_reserve (static) vs credit_smoothing (dynamic)?
Sam: plan suggestion:
1) add feature flag short_reserve_percent (canary = 0.15)
2) add feature flag credit_smoothing_enabled (canary false)
3) add per-tenant long_token_cap (canary 2048)
4) instrument: short-path P50/95/99, KV hit-rate, batch size distribution, kernel-selection ratio (fast/fallback)
5) run 2h mixed workload (50k short reqs/min, 2k long seqs/min) compare baseline/canaries
Tia: can you include metrics dashboards and alert thresholds you want?
Sam: metrics:
- short_p95_ms (goal < 60ms)
- short_p99_ms (goal < 200ms)
- kv_hit_rate_short (baseline 87%)
- kernel_fastpath_ratio (want > 90% for short requests)
alerts: short_p95 > baseline * 1.5 -> rollback
Mike: also add a microbenchmark that pins CPU/GPU kernel selection for short inputs to validate kernel swap cost. I can prepare kernels A/B test.
PerfBot: CI perf job queued: perf/canary-short-reserve-1719504321. Results ETA ~ 30m.
Leo: note for experiment log: capture tenant id correlation. Some tenants are naturally long-heavy; we should avoid penalizing them permanently. rolling window cap better than hard cap.
Sam: thanks — I'll wire flags and a short A/B harness this afternoon. ping me if you want to join pairing fam. :thumbsup:
Anya: thanks Sam. assign owners? Sam -> implement, Mike -> kernel microbench, Leo -> KV telemetry, Tia -> rollout/runbook. I'll take evaluation dashboard.
Sam: assigned. starting work now. will post PR + canary links.
Tia: also add a runbook step: if P95 spike persists, enable emergency short-only fastlane (drain long queue) and scale dedicated short-path capacity.
Mike: one more: consider lowering batcher.wait_ms for short-lane to reduce aggregation window. small values trade throughput for latency but might be fine for short tokens.
Sam: noted. will try wait_ms_short = 2ms in experiment.
PerfBot: perf/canary-short-reserve-1719504321 finished: short_p95 reduced 2.8x with short_reserve=0.15 vs baseline; KV hit recovered partially. Full report: https://perf.internal/report/1719504321
Anya: nice! post PR & TLDR so everyone can skim, then we can iterate on smoothing approach. :tada:
Sam: will do.
